title: Where did every drop go?
question: Can obstacle geometry predict which routes finite rain can take while every unit remains accounted for?
method: Fixed two-dimensional circle obstacles, analytic openings, independent flood-fill predictions, integer water ledgers and two grid resolutions.
finding: The recorded open cases drained, the blocked case retained and rejected water without drain leakage, and both resolutions kept explicit accounts.
claim_scope: Finite uncalibrated2D flow and restart experiments; no claim of realistic soil, physical seconds or3D packing.
limitations: Stationary overlapping-circle obstacles; prescribed transfer order, no grain movement, pressure, capillarity, momentum or evaporation.
Resolution changes alter represented solid area, accessible capacity and drainage amounts.
Zero leakage in the fixed2D model does not prove a sealed3D granular packing.
Original scientific results are retained reports; publication did not rerun the experiment. Selected files are not the complete raw evidence archive.
open_questions: Which quantities remain stable under further refinement, and where does the discrete geometry change the route?
